ろうちゅうしょうにん

p.src: Now, as Concubine Zhao was in her room complaining about Jia Huan, Jia Huan could be heard protesting in the outer room: “All I did was knock over the medicine pot and spill a little medicine. The girl did not die on the spot, yet he cursed me, and now you are cursing me too. You accuse me of being wicked and torment me as if you wanted me dead. Just wait—tomorrow I shall take that little girl’s life after all, and then we shall see what you can do! They had better be on their guard, that is all.” Concubine Zhao hurried out from the inner room, clapped a hand over his mouth, and said, “Will you go on spouting such wicked nonsense? You will have them taking my life first!” Mother and son quarreled for a while. After hearing what Xifeng had said, Concubine Zhao grew angrier the more she thought about it and did not even send anyone to offer Xifeng a word of comfort. A few days later, Qiaojie also recovered. Thus the enmity between the two sides grew deeper than ever.

p.src: One day Lin Zhixiao came in and reported, “Today is the Prince of Beijing’s birthday. What are your instructions, sir?” Jia Zheng instructed him, “Simply make the arrangements according to the custom of previous years. Inform the elder master and send the gifts over.” Lin Zhixiao assented and went off to make the arrangements. Before long Jia She came to consult with Jia Zheng, and they took Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, and Baoyu with them to offer birthday greetings to the Prince of Beijing. The others thought little of it, but Baoyu had always admired the Prince of Beijing’s handsome bearing and dignity and wished he could see him often. He therefore hurriedly changed his clothes and followed the others to the prince’s residence. Jia She and Jia Zheng presented their calling cards bearing their official titles and waited for the prince’s command. Before long a eunuch emerged, fingering a string of prayer beads. When he saw Jia She and Jia Zheng, he said with a broad smile, “Are you both well, my lords?” Jia She and Jia Zheng hastened to return his greeting. The three younger men also came forward and greeted him. The eunuch said, “His Highness bids you enter.” The five, elders and juniors together, followed the eunuch into the residence. They passed through two sets of gates and went around a hall before reaching the gate of the inner palace. On reaching the gate, they all halted while the eunuch went in first to announce them to the prince. The young eunuchs stationed at the gate came forward to greet them. Presently the eunuch came out and said, “Please.” The five men followed him in with solemn respect. They saw the Prince of Beijing, dressed in ceremonial robes, already waiting beneath the gallery at the entrance to the hall. Jia She and Jia Zheng stepped forward first to pay their respects, followed in order by Zhen, Lian, and Baoyu. The Prince of Beijing took Baoyu alone by the hand and said, “I have not seen you for a long time and have often thought of you.” Then he asked with a smile, “And is that jade of yours well?” Baoyu bowed and made a half-kneeling salute. “Thanks to Your Highness’s protection, all is well,” he replied. The Prince of Beijing said, “Now that you have come today, I have nothing especially good to offer you, so let us simply sit and talk together.” As he spoke, several eunuchs raised the curtain. Saying, “Please,” the Prince of Beijing entered first, after which Jia She and the others followed, walking with bowed bodies. First Jia She asked the Prince of Beijing to accept their formal homage. The prince offered a few modest demurrals, but Jia She had already knelt; Jia Zheng and the others then performed their salutations in order, as may be readily imagined.

p.src: Jia She and the others then withdrew with due solemnity. The Prince of Beijing ordered the eunuchs to seat them with the other relatives and old acquaintances and entertain them well. Baoyu alone he kept behind to talk with him, granting him a seat as well. Baoyu kowtowed once more in gratitude, then sat sideways on an embroidered stool near the door and conversed for a while about his studies, composition, and related matters. The Prince of Beijing showed him the greatest affection and had tea served to him. Then he said, “Yesterday Governor Wu came for an imperial audience. He spoke of how, when your honored father formerly served as Provincial Director of Education, he conducted affairs impartially and won the wholehearted respect of every licentiate and young scholar. During his audience His Majesty also asked about your father, and Governor Wu recommended him most warmly. This must surely be an auspicious sign for your honored father.” Baoyu hastened to rise. Only after hearing him out did he reply respectfully, “This is due to Your Highness’s gracious favor and Governor Wu’s great kindness.” While they were speaking, a young eunuch entered and reported, “The assembled officials and gentlemen outside are in the front hall, thanking Your Highness for the banquet.” With this, he presented their cards thanking the prince for the feast and wishing him well at midday. The Prince of Beijing glanced at them, handed them back to the young eunuch, and said with a smile, “Very well. It was kind of them to take the trouble.” The young eunuch reported further, “The meal Your Highness has specially bestowed upon Jia Baoyu is ready.” The Prince of Beijing ordered the eunuch to conduct Baoyu to a small but exquisitely appointed courtyard, where someone was assigned to accompany him at his meal. After eating, Baoyu returned to give thanks. After a few more kindly words, the Prince of Beijing suddenly said with a smile, “When I last saw that jade of yours, I found it most intriguing. On returning home, I described its design and had my craftsmen make one like it. Since you happen to be here today, take it home with you as a plaything.” He ordered a young eunuch to fetch it and handed it to Baoyu with his own hands. Baoyu received it in both hands, thanked him again, and then withdrew. The Prince of Beijing sent two young eunuchs out with him, and only then did Baoyu return home with Jia She and the others. Jia She then went back to his own apartments.

p.src: Meanwhile, Jia Zheng took the three younger men to see Grandmother Jia. After paying their respects, they spoke for a while about the people they had met at the prince’s residence. Baoyu also told Jia Zheng what he had heard about Governor Wu recommending him during his imperial audience. Jia Zheng said, “Governor Wu has long been a good friend of ours. He is one of our own circle and, as it happens, a man of integrity.” After a few more casual remarks, Grandmother Jia said, “Go and rest now.” Jia Zheng withdrew, while Zhen, Lian, and Baoyu accompanied him as far as the door. Jia Zheng said, “Go back, all of you, and keep the old lady company.” With that, he returned to his own room. He had barely been seated when a young maid came in and reported, “Lin Zhixiao is outside and requests permission to report to you, sir.” As she spoke, she handed him a red calling card bearing the name of Governor Wu. Jia Zheng understood that the governor had come to call and told the young maid to summon Lin Zhixiao. Jia Zheng went out beneath the veranda eaves. Lin Zhixiao entered and reported, “Governor Wu came to call today, but I told him you were unavailable, and he left. I have also heard that a vacancy for a director has arisen in the Ministry of Works, and people both outside and within the ministry are all saying that you, sir, are to be formally appointed to it.” Jia Zheng said, “We shall see.” Lin Zhixiao reported a few other matters before taking his leave.

p.src: To resume our story, Jia Zhen, Jia Lian, and Baoyu returned home. Baoyu alone went to Grandmother Jia's apartments, where he related how the Prince of Beijing had treated him and brought out the piece of jade. Everyone looked at it and laughed for a while. Grandmother Jia then ordered a servant, “Put it away for him, and mind that it isn't lost.” Then she asked, “You are keeping your own jade safely on you, aren't you? Don't get the two mixed up.” Baoyu took his jade from around his neck and said, “Isn't this my own jade? How could I possibly lose it? The two pieces are far too different to be confused with each other. I was just going to tell you, Grandmother: the other night, when I went to bed, I took off my jade and hung it inside the bed curtains. It actually began to glow, turning the whole canopy red.” Grandmother Jia said, “There you go talking nonsense again. The valance of your bed curtains is red, so naturally it looked red in the firelight.” “No,” said Baoyu. “The lamp had already gone out, and the room was pitch-dark, yet I could still see it.” Lady Xing and Lady Wang pursed their lips to suppress their laughter. Xifeng said, “It is a happy omen beginning to manifest itself.” “What happy omen?” Baoyu asked. Grandmother Jia said, “You wouldn't understand. You have been bustling about all day. Go and rest, and stop talking foolishness here.” Baoyu lingered a little longer before returning to the Garden.

p.src: Grandmother Jia then asked, “Ah, yes. When you went to visit Aunt Xue, did you mention this matter?” Lady Wang replied, “We had meant to go earlier, but Xifeng was occupied with Qiaojie's illness, so we were delayed for two days and did not go until today. We told Aunt Xue everything. She was very willing, but said that Pan is away from home just now and, since his father is no longer alive, she must discuss it with him before proceeding.” Grandmother Jia said, “That is only reasonable. In that case, none of us should mention it for now. We shall wait until your aunt has reached a decision with her family.” Leaving Grandmother Jia and the others to discuss the marriage, we turn to Baoyu, who returned to his room and told Xiren, “Grandmother and Sister Xifeng were speaking so obscurely just now that I couldn't make out what they meant.” Xiren thought for a moment, then smiled and said, “I cannot guess either. But when they said those things just now, was Miss Lin present?” Baoyu replied, “Miss Lin has only just recovered from her illness. She hasn't been to Grandmother's apartments at all lately.” As they spoke, they heard Sheyue and Qiuwen quarrelling in the outer room. Xiren called, “What are you two squabbling about now?” Sheyue replied, “We were playing cards. When she won my money, she took it, but when she lost, she refused to pay. That would have been bad enough, but then she snatched away all the rest of my money as well.” Baoyu laughed. “What do a few coins matter, you silly girls? Stop quarrelling.” At this, the two girls went and sat down, both pouting sulkily. Xiren then settled Baoyu in bed. We need say no more of this.

p.src: Now Xiren, having heard what Baoyu had said, knew perfectly well that the matter concerned a marriage proposal for him. But she feared that Baoyu, forever prone to foolish fancies, would be prompted into all manner of absurd remarks if the subject were raised. She therefore pretended not to understand, though in her own mind it was a matter of the utmost concern. As she lay in bed that night, an idea came to her: she might as well visit Zijuan and see whether anything seemed to be afoot there; then she would naturally learn the truth. Early the next morning, after seeing Baoyu off to school, she washed and dressed, then made her way slowly to the Naiad's House. She found Zijuan there pinching off flowers. When Zijuan saw Xiren enter, she greeted her with a cheerful smile: “Do come inside and sit down, Sister.” “Thank you,” said Xiren. “Are you picking flowers, little sister? Where is your young mistress?” Zijuan replied, “Miss has just finished washing and dressing and is waiting for her medicine to be warmed.” As she spoke, Zijuan led Xiren inside. They found Daiyu reading a book. Xiren said with an ingratiating smile, “No wonder you tire your mind, Miss, when you begin reading the moment you rise. How wonderful it would be if our Master Bao studied as diligently as you do!” Daiyu smiled and put down her book. Xueyan entered carrying a small tea tray with a cup of medicine and a cup of water upon it, followed by a young maid bearing a spittoon and a rinsing bowl. Xiren had come intending to sound them out, but after sitting for a while she could find no opening. Then she reflected that Daiyu was exceptionally sensitive: if she failed to discover anything and only succeeded in upsetting her, that would be worse still. So she remained a little longer, made some polite conversation, and took her leave. As she approached the entrance to Happy Red Court, she saw two people standing there. Xiren thought it improper to go any closer, but one of them had already seen her and hurried over. Xiren saw that it was Chuyao and asked, “What are you doing here?” Chuyao replied, “Second Master Yun came just now with a note for our Master Bao to read. He is waiting here for an answer.” Xiren said, “Master Bao goes to school every day. Surely you know that. What answer is there to wait for?” Chuyao smiled. “I told him so. He asked me to tell you and said he would wait for your reply.” Xiren was about to reply when she saw the other man edging slowly toward them. Looking carefully, she recognized Jia Yun, who was sidling over in a hesitant, furtive manner. Seeing that it was Jia Yun, Xiren hastily told Chuyao, “Tell him I understand. We shall show it to Master Bao when he returns.” Jia Yun had originally meant to come over and speak to Xiren, merely from a wish to be friendly, but he dared not presume and could only approach at a slow pace. He was already quite near when, unexpectedly, Xiren said this. Unable to advance any farther without embarrassment, he stopped where he was. Xiren had already turned her back on him and was making her way inside.

p.src: That evening, when Baoyu returned to his room, Xiren reported, “Second Master Yun came to the corridor today.” “What did he want?” asked Baoyu. “He left a note for you,” said Xiren. “Where is it? Bring it here and let me see it.” Sheyue went into the inner room and fetched it from the top of the bookcase. Baoyu took it and saw that the wrapper bore the words, “A respectful message to my honored uncle.” “Why has the boy stopped acknowledging me as his father again?” Baoyu asked. “What do you mean?” asked Xiren. Baoyu said, “When he gave me those white begonias the year before last, he addressed me as his ‘honored father.’ Today he has written ‘uncle’ on the wrapper. Does that not mean he has disowned me again?” Xiren said, “Neither he nor you has any sense of shame. A grown man like him acknowledging someone your age as his father—is that not shameless of him? And you do not even properly have a—” At this point she blushed and smiled faintly. Baoyu understood her meaning and said, “That is hard to say. As the proverb says, ‘A monk may have no sons, yet he has no lack of dutiful children.’ I only treated him that way because he seemed clever and likable. If he does not want it, I have no great desire for him either.” As he spoke, he opened the note. Xiren laughed and said, “Second Master Yun is rather furtive too. One moment he wants to see someone, and the next he is hiding away. He must be a rather devious fellow.” Baoyu was intent on opening and reading the letter and paid no attention to Xiren’s remarks. As Xiren watched him read, he frowned for a while, then smiled, then shook his head, until at last he appeared thoroughly vexed. When he had finished, Xiren asked, “What is it about?” Baoyu gave no answer but tore the note into several pieces. Seeing this, Xiren did not press him and merely asked whether he meant to study after dinner. Baoyu said, “It is absurd that Yun should be such a scoundrel.” Seeing that his answer had nothing to do with her question, Xiren smiled slightly and asked, “But what is it really about?” “Why bother asking about him?” said Baoyu. “Let us eat. After dinner, let us rest. My mind is in such turmoil that I am thoroughly vexed.” Then he told a young maid to bring a light and burned the torn pieces of the note.

Baoyu was intent on opening and reading the letter and paid no attention to Xiren’s remarks.
As Xiren watched him read, he frowned for a while, then smiled, then shook his head, until at last he appeared thoroughly vexed.
When he had finished, Xiren asked, “What is it about?”
Baoyu gave no answer but tore the note into several pieces. Seeing this, Xiren did not press him and merely asked whether he meant to study after dinner.
Baoyu said, “It is absurd that Yun should be such a scoundrel.”
Seeing that his answer had nothing to do with her question, Xiren smiled slightly and asked, “But what is it really about?”
“Why bother asking about him?” said Baoyu. “Let us eat.
After dinner, let us rest. My mind is in such turmoil that I am thoroughly vexed.”
Then he told a young maid to bring a light and burned the torn pieces of the note.

p.src: Presently the young maids served dinner. Baoyu merely sat there in a daze. Xiren coaxed and teased him until he ate a mouthful, but then he put down his bowl and lay gloomily upon the bed once more. After a while, tears suddenly began to fall from his eyes. Neither Xiren nor Sheyue could make head or tail of it. Sheyue said, “Everything was perfectly fine, so what is the matter now? Some Yun or Yu or whoever he may be sends this wretched note about goodness knows what, and it has made you act like a simpleton—crying one moment and laughing the next. If this everlasting guessing game goes on day after day, how are we supposed to bear it?” As she spoke, she actually grew distressed herself. Xiren could not help laughing beside her and tried to soothe her: “Dear sister, do not upset everyone further. He is already more than enough for us to contend with, and now you are behaving like this too. Surely whatever was in that note had nothing to do with you?” “Now you are talking nonsense,” said Sheyue. Who knows what outrageous things were written in his note? Do not drag other people into it at random. If that is how you put it, I should think the note was more likely about you.” Before Xiren could reply, they heard Baoyu burst out laughing on the bed. He scrambled up, shook out his clothes, and said, “Let us go to sleep and stop this quarrelling. I still have to rise early tomorrow to study.” With that, he lay down and went to sleep. Nothing further happened that night.

p.src: The next morning, Baoyu rose, washed and dressed, and set off for the family school. After stepping through the courtyard gate, he suddenly remembered something. He told Beiming to wait and hurried back, calling, “Where is Sister Sheyue?” Sheyue answered and came out to ask, “Why have you come back?” Baoyu said, “If Yun comes today, tell him not to make trouble here. If he does it again, I shall report him to Grandmother and Father.” Sheyue assented, and only then did Baoyu turn to leave. He had only just started out when he saw Jia Yun hurrying in. At the sight of Baoyu, Jia Yun promptly paid his respects and said, “Congratulations, Uncle!” Baoyu assumed that he meant the matter of the previous day and said, “You are far too reckless. You never care whether a person has troubles of his own; you simply come and pester him.” Jia Yun smiled ingratiatingly. “If you do not believe me, Uncle, go and see for yourself. Everyone is already here at our main gate.” Baoyu became still more alarmed. “What on earth are you talking about?” While they were speaking, a great clamor suddenly arose outside. “Do you hear that, Uncle?” said Jia Yun. Baoyu grew even more suspicious. Then he heard someone shout, “What appalling manners you people have! What sort of place do you think this is, making such a racket here?” Another man answered, “It is the master’s own fault for being promoted! How could you expect us not to come and make a festive noise? Other households long for such congratulations and cannot get them.” Only then did Baoyu realize that Jia Zheng had been promoted to Assistant Director and that these people had come to announce the glad tidings. Naturally, he was delighted. As he hurried away, Jia Yun caught up with him and said, “Are you happy, Uncle? And if your marriage should be settled as well, that would surely make it a double celebration.” Baoyu flushed, spat, and exclaimed, “Pah! You tiresome wretch! Why do you not go away at once?” Jia Yun blushed and said, “What is there in that? It seems to me, sir, that you simply do not—” Baoyu’s face darkened. “Simply do not what?” Before Jia Yun could finish, he lost the courage to say another word.

p.src: Baoyu entered the room smiling. Daiyu was seated close beside Grandmother Jia on her left, while Xiangyun sat on her right. Lady Xing and Lady Wang sat below them. Tanchun, Xichun, Li Wan, Xifeng, Li Wen, Li Qi, Xing Xiuyan, and all the other young ladies were in the room; only Baochai, Baoqin, and Yingchun were absent. Baoyu was so delighted that he could scarcely speak. He hastened to congratulate Grandmother Jia, then Lady Xing and Lady Wang, and greeted each of the young ladies in turn. At last he smiled at Daiyu and asked, “Are you quite recovered now, little cousin?” Daiyu smiled faintly too. “Quite recovered. I heard that you had been unwell too, Second Cousin. Are you better now?” “Indeed I am,” said Baoyu. “That night my heart suddenly began to ache. I had only just improved these past few days before returning to school, so I could not come to see you.” Before he had finished, Daiyu had already turned away to speak to Tanchun. Standing below, Xifeng laughed. “You two hardly seem to be together every day. You behave more like guests, exchanging all these courtesies. This must be what people call ‘treating one another with the respect due a guest.’” Everyone laughed at this. Lin Daiyu flushed crimson. Unable either to answer or to remain silent, she hesitated a while before saying, “What do you know about it?” This made them laugh all the more. Only then did Xifeng grasp the implication of her own words and realize that she had spoken rashly. She was just about to change the subject when Baoyu suddenly said to Daiyu, “Cousin Lin, just look what a blundering fool Yun is.” No sooner had he said it than he remembered, and fell silent. Everyone burst out laughing again and asked, “Where did that come from?” Daiyu could make neither head nor tail of it and joined them in an embarrassed laugh. At a loss for anything else to say, Baoyu added, “By the way, I just heard that someone is sending an opera troupe. What day did they say it would be?” They all looked at him and laughed. Xifeng said, “You heard it outside, so you should be telling us. Whom are you asking now?” Seizing the opportunity, Baoyu said, “I shall go outside and ask again.” Grandmother Jia said, “Do not run outside. For one thing, the messengers announcing the good news are a ridiculous sight; for another, today is a day of great joy for your father, and if he comes back and runs into you, he will only lose his temper again.” Baoyu answered, “Yes,” and only then went out.

p.src: Grandmother Jia then asked Xifeng who had spoken of sending the opera troupe. Xifeng replied, “They say the message came from His Lordship, Uncle Wang. The day after tomorrow is auspicious, so he is sending a newly formed troupe of young players to congratulate you, Master Jia, and Lady Wang.” Then she added with a smile, “It is not merely an auspicious day—it is a very special day as well.” As she said this, she looked at Daiyu and smiled. Daiyu smiled faintly too. Lady Wang said, “Why, of course—the day after tomorrow is our niece’s special day too.” Grandmother Jia thought for a moment and laughed. “This shows how old I have grown; I am muddled about everything now. Fortunately, I have this girl Feng to serve as my personal remembrancer. Since that is so, it works out splendidly: her uncle’s family will congratulate them, while your uncle’s family will celebrate your birthday. Could anything be better?” Everyone laughed and said, “Every word our Old Ancestress speaks is perfectly reasoned. No wonder you enjoy such great blessings.” As they spoke, Baoyu came in. Hearing all this, he was so delighted that he fairly danced for joy. Before long, they all dined in Grandmother Jia’s apartments, amid great merriment that need not be described. p.src: Two days passed in this fashion, and the day of celebration arrived. Early that morning, Wang Ziteng and the other relatives sent over a theatrical troupe, and a temporary stage was erected before Grandmother Jia's main hall. Outside, the gentlemen all attended in their official robes, while the relatives who had come with congratulations filled more than ten banquet tables. Within, since the plays were new and Grandmother Jia was in high spirits, a glazed theatrical screen was set up to partition off the rear hall, where banquet tables were laid as well. At the table in the place of honor sat Aunt Xue, accompanied by Lady Wang and Baoqin; opposite, at the old lady's table, sat Lady Xing and Xiuyan. Two tables farther down were still empty, so Grandmother Jia told them to hurry the others along. Before long, Xifeng appeared at the head of the maids, all of them clustered around Lin Daiyu. Daiyu had changed into several fresh garments and was adorned like Chang'e descending to the mortal world; shyly smiling, she came forward to greet everyone. Xiangyun, Li Wen, and Li Wan all urged her to take the seat of honor, but Daiyu steadfastly refused. Grandmother Jia laughed. “You must sit there today.” Aunt Xue rose and asked, “Is there some happy occasion for Miss Lin today as well?” Grandmother Jia replied with a smile, “It is her birthday.” “Oh!” said Aunt Xue. “I had quite forgotten.” She went over to Daiyu and said, “Forgive my poor memory. Later I shall have Baoqin come and offer you birthday greetings.” Daiyu smiled and said, “You are too kind.” Everyone took their seats. Daiyu looked carefully around and, noticing that Baochai alone was absent, asked, “Is Sister Bao well? Why has she not come?” Aunt Xue replied, “She ought to have come, but there was no one to watch the house, so she stayed behind.” Blushing, Daiyu said with a faint smile, “But Aunt, now that you have a new daughter-in-law at home, why must Sister Bao be the one to mind the house? I expect she finds crowds and commotion tiresome and simply could not be bothered to come. I have been missing her very much.” Aunt Xue laughed. “How good of you to keep her in your thoughts. She often thinks of all you sisters too. In a day or so I shall send her over, and you can all have a good talk together.”

In the third, they saw a Golden Boy and Jade Maiden bearing banners and jeweled canopies, leading on a young female-role performer clad in rainbow skirts and feathered robes, with a black veil over her head. p.src: Just as everyone was enjoying themselves, a servant from the Xue household suddenly burst in, his head drenched with sweat, and said to Xue Ke, “Second Master, hurry home! Send word inside to Madam as well and ask her to return at once. Something urgent has happened at home.” “What has happened?” asked Xue Ke. “I will tell you when we get home,” replied the servant. Without even taking time to say farewell, Xue Ke hurried away. When Aunt Xue received the message relayed by the maids inside, she was even more terrified, her face turning ashen. She rose in haste, took Baoqin with her, uttered a hurried farewell, and at once boarded her carriage and returned home. Everyone inside and out was left bewildered. Grandmother Jia said, “Let us send someone after them to learn what has really happened. We are all concerned.” Everyone answered, “Yes.” We shall leave the Jia household to continue watching the plays and speak only of Aunt Xue's return home. There she found two constables standing at the inner gate, accompanied by several clerks from the pawnshop, who were saying, “Once Madam returns, the matter can be properly dealt with.” As they were speaking, Aunt Xue came in. When the constables saw an elderly lady surrounded by a large retinue of men and women, they knew that she must be Xue Pan's mother. Overawed by such an imposing display, they did not dare make any trouble, but could only stand respectfully with hands lowered and let Aunt Xue pass inside.

p.src: When Aunt Xue reached the back of the reception hall, she could already hear someone wailing. It was Jingui. Aunt Xue hurried over and saw Baochai coming out to meet her, her face streaked with tears. At the sight of Aunt Xue, she said, “Mother, try not to be alarmed when you hear. What matters now is dealing with the situation.” Aunt Xue went into the room with Baochai. On her way in she had already overheard the servants talking, and was trembling with fright. Weeping, she asked, “Who was it, after all?” One of the servants replied, “Madam need not ask about the particulars just now. Whoever it was, a life must be paid for when a man has been beaten to death. We had better decide what to do first.” Aunt Xue came out weeping and said, “What is there left to discuss?” The servant said, “In our humble opinion, we should prepare some silver tonight and hurry away with Second Master to meet Eldest Master. Once there, we can seek out an experienced legal clerk and promise him some money, so that he may first find a way to disentangle Eldest Master from the capital charge. Then, on returning, we can ask the Jia family to intercede with the higher authorities. As for the runners waiting outside, Madam should first give us a few taels of silver with which to send them away. Then we can hurry on with the business.” Aunt Xue said, “Find the dead man’s family and promise them money for the funeral, as well as something for their support. If the complainants cease pressing the charge, the matter will ease.” From behind the curtain Baochai said, “Mother, you mustn’t. In affairs like this, the more money you give, the greater the trouble becomes. What the young servant said just now is the right course.” Aunt Xue wept again. “I no longer care whether I live or die. I shall hurry there, see him once, and die together with him, and that will be the end of it.” In desperation Baochai tried to console her, while calling from behind the curtain, “Hurry and go with Second Master to see to it.” The maids supported Aunt Xue into the room. Just as Xue Ke was about to leave, Baochai said, “As soon as there is any news, send someone back with it at once. You need only attend to matters out there.” Xue Ke assented and left. Baochai had only just begun consoling Aunt Xue when Jingui seized Xiangling in an unguarded moment and shouted at her again, “You people are always boasting that someone in their family beat a man to death and nothing happened to him—he simply came to the capital. Now, after all your urging, someone really has been beaten to death. Ordinarily you speak only of having money, influence, and powerful relations, yet now I see that even you are scared out of your wits and running about in confusion. If anything happens to Eldest Master tomorrow and he cannot return, each of you will go off about your own affairs and leave me here alone to suffer!” With that, she burst into loud sobs again. When Aunt Xue heard this, her anger and distress made her even more faint. Baochai was at her wits’ end. Amid all this commotion, a senior maid arrived from the Jia household; Lady Wang had already sent her to inquire what had happened.

u.src: When Aunt Xue reached the back of the reception hall, she could already hear someone wailing. It was Jingui.

Aunt Xue hurried over and saw Baochai coming out to meet her, her face streaked with tears. At the sight of Aunt Xue, she said, “Mother, try not to be alarmed when you hear. What matters now is dealing with the situation.”
Aunt Xue went into the room with Baochai. On her way in she had already overheard the servants talking, and was trembling with fright. Weeping, she asked, “Who was it, after all?”
One of the servants replied, “Madam need not ask about the particulars just now. Whoever it was, a life must be paid for when a man has been beaten to death. We had better decide what to do first.”
Aunt Xue came out weeping and said, “What is there left to discuss?”

The servant said, “In our humble opinion, we should prepare some silver tonight and hurry away with Second Master to meet Eldest Master. Once there, we can seek out an experienced legal clerk and promise him some money, so that he may first find a way to disentangle Eldest Master from the capital charge. Then, on returning, we can ask the Jia family to intercede with the higher authorities.
As for the runners waiting outside, Madam should first give us a few taels of silver with which to send them away.
Then we can hurry on with the business.”
Aunt Xue said, “Find the dead man’s family and promise them money for the funeral, as well as something for their support. If the complainants cease pressing the charge, the matter will ease.”
From behind the curtain Baochai said, “Mother, you mustn’t.
In affairs like this, the more money you give, the greater the trouble becomes. What the young servant said just now is the right course.”
Aunt Xue wept again. “I no longer care whether I live or die. I shall hurry there, see him once, and die together with him, and that will be the end of it.”

With that, she burst into loud sobs again.
When Aunt Xue heard this, her anger and distress made her even more faint.
Baochai was at her wits’ end.
Amid all this commotion, a senior maid arrived from the Jia household; Lady Wang had already sent her to inquire what had happened.

p.src: Although Baochai knew in her heart that she was now to be one of the Jia family, the matter had not yet been formally announced; and with the situation so urgent, she could only say to the senior maid, “At present we do not yet know the whole story. We have heard only that my elder brother beat a man to death while away from home and has been arrested by the county authorities. We do not know what sentence he will receive. Second Master has only just gone to make inquiries. As soon as we receive definite news, perhaps later today, we shall promptly send word to your mistress. Please go back first and thank her for her concern. From now on there will be so much for which we must rely upon the gentlemen of your household.” The maid acknowledged her words and left. Aunt Xue and Baochai remained at home, unable to think what to do.

u.src: Two days later, the young servant returned with a letter, which he handed to a little maid to carry inside.
When Baochai opened it, the letter read:

p.src: The death caused by Elder Brother was accidental injury, not intentional killing. This morning I submitted an additional petition in my own name, but no ruling has yet been issued. Elder Brother’s earlier deposition was exceedingly unfavorable. Once this petition is approved, he will be examined again; if he can revise his testimony convincingly, his life may be spared. Quickly obtain another five hundred taels of silver from the pawnshop for expenses. On no account delay. And please tell Mother not to worry. Ask the young servant about everything else.

p.src: After reading the letter, Baochai read every word of it aloud to Aunt Xue. Wiping away her tears, Aunt Xue said, “Judging by this, whether he lives or dies is still uncertain.” Baochai said, “Mother, do not grieve yet. Let us call the young servant in and learn the particulars before we say more.” As she spoke, she sent a little maid to summon him inside. Aunt Xue asked him, “Tell me in detail what happened to Eldest Master.” The young servant said, “That night, when I heard what Eldest Master and Second Master were saying, I was so frightened that my wits deserted me.” What the young servant had to tell will be revealed in the next chapter.
